output.brief:
I can't yet say that the new night rota caused the rise in falls, and I would not recommend reversing it or halting the rollout now.

What the evidence shows: the rise coincides with the switch to the incident app on 1 July. Q2 was an unusually low quarter at both homes, near the bottom of their history. Handover notes show some Q2 falls were never written up. The growth is concentrated in no-harm and "found on floor" events, while serious falls (GP or hospital attendance) barely moved, from 2 to 3. Q3 rates sit inside the homes' long-run limits. Other homes have had similar jumps that reversed.

What I can't rule out: a real rota effect, frailer admissions, or medication changes. A sustained 40% rise would take 2–3 quarters to show on the chart. We have no pre-June call-bell data. Ashby Fold answers a median of 3m40s, but there is nothing to compare it with. Penmor Lodge's call system can't record answer times at all.

Next steps: keep the pilot running under its pause criteria. Show falls as rates on the control chart, with the reporting change marked. Start manual sampling of night call-bell response times now. Track admissions' frailty and medication changes. Decide on the rollout at a dated review in late January using Q4 data. Don't discipline staff, and don't withdraw the app.
